05 ADHD and sleep · class card

Orexin antagonists

orexin receptor antagonists · suvorexant

Practice
  1. 24-year-old man with narcolepsy on modafinil asks for a sleep aid: lies awake 2 hours most nights for a month sleep hygiene reviewed; no alcohol or opioids; no depression examination normal · urine drug screen negative → Suvorexant → suvorexant blocks orexin receptors, and narcolepsy can stem from orexin deficiency, so it is contraindicated; cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia comes first, and zolpidem acts at the benzodiazepine site
  2. 47-year-old woman on suvorexant for chronic insomnia drowsy and slow at work for 4 days began clarithromycin-based Helicobacter pylori therapy 5 days ago same nightly dose · 8 hours in bed · no alcohol · examination normal → Clarithromycin raising the suvorexant level → clarithromycin blocks cytochrome P450 3A4, the enzyme that clears suvorexant, so exposure climbs and sleepiness carries into the day; she drinks no alcohol and spends a full night in bed
  3. 58-year-old man with decompensated cirrhosis from hepatitis C wakes at 3 AM and cannot fall back asleep, most nights for 6 months asks for a sleeping pill; no alcohol for 2 years ascites · jaundice · no asterixis → Suvorexant → an orexin antagonist is not recommended in liver disease, and decompensated cirrhosis is the severe impairment its label names; stimulus control and sleep restriction are behavioral parts of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia
